clue.text: Subsection of right infiltrating activist group

indicators.note: to infiltrate a group is to get inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a faction is a dissenting group within a party
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A wing of a political party has been infiltrated by right-wing militants.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a small part or portion broken off from a whole, much like a subsection.

clue.text: Cut cakes up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: buns are small sweet cakes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests slicing cakes; 'Cut' is the definition in its social sense, ignoring someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore them deliberately in public, which is exactly a snub.

clue.text: Vicious recession has PM in shock

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid Vicious was the Sex Pistols' bassist
Theresa May was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A savage economic downturn leaves the Prime Minister reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious' reads as an adjective for the recession, but it is the punk bassist Sid Vicious of the Sex Pistols, and 'recession' turns his first name round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a sudden feeling of alarm and distress, the same emotional jolt as shock.

clue.text: Proper game between Portugal and Germany is hard

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
RU is rugby union
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture played between Portugal and Germany proves a tough contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The game sits between the two country codes, which in this case is simply their reading order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prudish is excessively concerned with decorum and propriety, overly correct or prim in manner.

clue.text: Long time getting round variety of bar's ports!

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: hours can mean a long time, as in 'it took hours'

indicators.note: a variety offers a different version, so these letters come in a new order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A long pub crawl round several bars serving port wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Harbours are sheltered coastal places where ships dock, which is what ports are.

clue.text: Helpful to owl with her hatch

indicators.note: to hatch a plan is to devise or contrive it, so the letters are worked into something new

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand to a mother owl as her eggs hatch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthwhile repays the effort spent, so it is useful or beneficial, that is, helpful.

clue.text: Strict with reduced number joining regiment

indicators.note: a reduced word has been cut short, so its final letter goes

parts.note: one particular number
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A disciplinarian officer with a depleted unit joining the regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is any number you need; seven loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and strict both describe harsh, uncompromising discipline or rules that permit no leniency.

clue.text: Fellow run out by new opener has row on boundary

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the initial letter of the word
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a batsman is run out by the new opener and there's a row about whether the ball reached the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words (run out, opener, boundary) all pull together, but only 'boundary' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the border line separating two countries, which is a boundary.

clue.text: Inspired one with zero knowledge

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a dog'
W is the abbreviation for with
the figure zero looks like O
ken is knowledge or understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: An inspired person is someone with no knowledge at all, an ironic picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that have been awoken have been stirred or roused, in the way that inspired emotions are.

clue.text: Strike-breaker finally arrives by taxi

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A worker who crosses the picket line finally turns up by taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Scab is a contemptuous term for a worker who keeps working during a strike, breaking it.

clue.text: Cured crazy online gambler?

parts.note: mad means crazy
E as in e-mail stands for electronic, online
a better is one who bets

explanation.surface: Has an obsessive internet gambler been cured of the habit?
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who has been healed of an illness has been restored to health, so made better.

clue.text: Rotten to hit fly carelessly

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters land in a sloppy new order

parts.note: six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Swatting a fly carelessly is a rotten thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal ways of calling something nasty or very unpleasant, as in filthy weather.

clue.text: Marry ultimately perfect man in Windsor, for example?

indicators.note: the pieces before this word go inside the item named after it

parts.note: a Windsor is a type of necktie knot

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A perfect man at Windsor, perhaps a royal bridegroom, is ready to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: Windsor suggests the castle and royal weddings, but the Windsor is a broad necktie knot; T and HE go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie the knot is an informal idiom meaning to get married.

clue.text: Screeched, as second tremor trapped wife and daughter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one letter sits within another word

parts.note: a quake is a tremor
W is the abbreviation for wife
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A wife and daughter, trapped by an aftershock, screamed for help.
explanation.definitionFit: To squawk is to give a loud harsh cry like a bird, so squawked means screeched.

clue.text: Doctor even has student work to cover

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, changing its arrangement

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Even a doctor has student work to mark, or to cover for a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop something is to wrap or surround it completely, which is to cover it.

clue.text: Outside broadcast gets player hitting first ball to spectator

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for outside broadcast
in tennis the server strikes the first ball of each point

explanation.surface: A TV outside broadcast catches a tennis player serving to a fan in the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer watches events without taking part, just as a spectator does.

clue.text: Hoping endlessly for painkiller

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: aspiring means hoping or aiming

explanation.surface: Someone with a headache longs endlessly for a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common over-the-counter drug taken to relieve pain, a standard analgesic.

clue.text: Abuse indulgence for being sick?

parts.note: being sick is being ill
a treat is an indulgence

explanation.surface: Is a little indulgence the right thing to give someone who is sick?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second part as 'a treat for the ill', with the pieces in reverse order to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat a person or animal is to handle them cruelly, the verb sense of abuse.

clue.text: Note who the French shot?

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
qui is French for who and la is French for the

explanation.surface: A query about whom the French executed by shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' applies to both words, so who and the are each translated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit commonly drunk as a single shot glass measure.

clue.text: I get she's desperate to visit as a tourist

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild or frantic, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone understands that she is desperate to go travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To sightsee is to go around looking at famous places and attractions, as holidaymakers do.

clue.text: Kind of trendy to take Alpha course

parts.note: in means fashionable
Alpha is the NATO phonetic word for A
a way is a course or route

explanation.surface: It's sort of fashionable to sign up for an Alpha course.
explanation.walkthrough: An Alpha course is a well-known introductory Christianity course in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal hedges meaning to some extent or partly, as in 'it was kind of sad'.

clue.text: Use new £1 after 1 March for breakfast

indicators.note: the number one before a word marks its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the month

indicators.note: a new version is a remade one, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
the pound sign is a stylised L, from Latin libra
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Spend a new pound coin after the first of March on something for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: '£1' and '1 March' look like a sum and a date; the pound sign gives L, 1 gives I, and the first of March is its initial M.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning meal.

clue.text: Humble poem breaks woman's sympathetic heart

indicators.note: something that breaks into a word forces its way inside it

parts.note: Ms is the title for a woman
an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of an eleven-letter word

explanation.surface: A poem breaks through to a woman's kind heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and humble both describe someone with a low estimate of their own importance or achievements.

clue.text: Setting for retreat's next to sports field

parts.note: to back away is to retreat
a ground is a sports field, as a cricket or football ground

explanation.surface: A country retreat set beside a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: The background of a story or picture is its scene or surroundings, that is, its setting.

clue.text: Backing up, luxury car makes vibrating sound

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the next word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
RR is Rolls-Royce, the luxury car maker

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce reversing makes a gentle engine hum.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat purrs by making a low continuous rumbling noise in the throat, a vibrating sound.

clue.text: Look both ways!

parts.note: surface reading: the road-safety command to check left and right before crossing
setter's reading: a word for a glance that reads the same whichever direction you take it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the kerbside instruction; read cryptically, it asks for a word meaning a glance that is spelt identically in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick or furtive glance, a brief look, and its letters form a palindrome.

clue.text: Try to persuade old king to protect a judge

indicators.note: to protect is to shield by surrounding, so one piece goes around the others

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
taken as written
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: Someone lobbies an elderly monarch to shield a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To cajole is to coax someone with flattery into doing something, which is trying to persuade.

clue.text: Left savage, southern waste for a better place in America

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: to lay waste is to wreck, so the letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a savage southern wilderness for a better life in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'improved' but means one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is famous for its casinos, so it is a place in the US for gamblers to visit.
